findings.description: Pending-file initialization happens in resolve_target before acquiring the target lock. Its existence check and truncating cat are not atomic.
findings.failure_mode: Two first-time writers target the same sprint. Writer A observes the pending file is absent and pauses. Writer B initializes it and successfully appends a row. A resumes and truncates the file to decisions: [], then acquires the lock and appends its own row. B's acknowledged decision disappears, and verification passes because A reads the already-truncated ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Acquire the target lock before checking for or initializing the pending file, and hold it through verification and replacement.

findings.description: Import locks only the destination ledger, reads a snapshot of the pending source, and later unconditionally deletes that source.
findings.failure_mode: A worktree writer appends a decision after import reads the pending file but before import removes it. Import commits only the earlier snapshot and then deletes the newly updated source, permanently losing the additional decision despite the writer reporting success.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate imports and pending writers with a shared source lock held from snapshot acquisition through source removal. Ensure lock identity is shared across checkouts and acquire source and destination locks in a consistent order.

findings.description: Confirmation allows a PRD-only unattended signal through live_run_signal, but derive_attribution immediately treats that same context as unattended and discards the operator's --answer-ref.
findings.failure_mode: After an autonomous run ends, a PRD whose Status still says autonomous causes an operator confirmation of an agent-proposed row with a null reference to persist decided_by: agent instead of operator. The confirmation reference is lost, and operator-owned decisions continue appearing in --not-decided-by operator reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate proposal-context detection from operator transition attribution. Once confirmation passes the live-run gate, validate and retain the operator reference even when the PRD still describes autonomous operation.

findings.description: Rejecting an agent-proposed replacement updates only the replacement row; it never clears the original decided row's supersede_proposed_by pointer.
findings.failure_mode: An agent proposes DEC-0002 to replace DEC-0001, then DEC-0002 is rejected. DEC-0001 still points to DEC-0002, so every subsequent agent supersede attempt fails with 'a replacement is already proposed'. The normal propose/reject/revise workflow cannot continue without operator intervention.
findings.suggested_fix: When rejecting a replacement, atomically clear its predecessor's supersede_proposed_by if it still points to the rejected ID, and include both rows in verification.

findings.description: op_confirm gates on live_run_signal (live kinds only) but then calls derive_attribution, which checks is_unattended, and that includes the PRD `**Status:**` signal (kind `prd`). With a PRD whose status line contains 'autonomous' or 'unattended' and no live signal, confirm is allowed to proceed, derive_attribution discards --answer-ref with a WARN (REF stays empty), the row's decided_by_ref stays null, and the jq in op_confirm sets decided_by = proposed_by, i.e. 'agent'. The operator's explicit confirmation is permanently recorded as an agent decision, which is the exact failure the ledger exists to prevent. decisions.md rule 3 promises the cli: ref 'is what records decided_by: operator'.
findings.failure_mode: Any project whose PRD status reads Autonomous/Unattended (the normal state for the autonomous-agent skill) produces decided rows attributed to 'agent' after operator confirm; `list --not-decided-by operator` and the SDD appendix D keep reporting them as agent decisions; the transition log says operator:decisions-command while the row says decided_by: agent, an inconsistency the append-only ledger can never repair.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the attribution gate match the confirm gate: in derive_attribution, when is_operator_call is true, treat only live_run_signal as 'unattended' (or pass a flag from op_confirm). Alternatively op_confirm should validate --answer-ref against REF_RE/OPREF_RE itself and set REF directly. Extend tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats confirm-under-PRD case to assert decided_by == operator and decided_by_ref == the cli: ref, not just status.

findings.description: Same is_unattended-vs-live_run_signal mismatch in the other operator paths. op_reject on a decided row dies when is_unattended is true, so a PRD-only signal makes operator rejection of decided rows impossible until the PRD text is edited. op_supersede uses `is_operator_call && ! is_unattended` to choose the operator path; under a PRD-only signal it silently falls to the agent path (old row gets supersede_proposed_by instead of status superseded), contradicting decisions.md ('The old row becomes superseded') and the 'a replacement is already proposed' refusal then applies to the operator too.
findings.failure_mode: Operator-typed /decisions reject on a decided row is refused with 'the context is unattended' on any repo whose PRD status mentions autonomous; operator supersede records the wrong transition shape without any message explaining why.
findings.suggested_fix: Use live_run_signal (not is_unattended) for the operator-path checks in op_reject and op_supersede, matching op_confirm; print the chosen path (operator vs agent) in the log line so a degraded path is visible.

findings.description: decided_by_ref is only set when currently null. A row proposed with --as flatline/dissent already carries decided_by_ref = flatline:<artifact>, so the operator's cli: ref is dropped on confirm and decided_by becomes 'flatline'/'dissent', never 'operator'. The grimoire-index comment ('Decided by = decided_by, or the proposing voice while the row awaits confirm') and decisions.md rule 3 both imply the confirming operator should be recorded. If this is intentional, the docs are wrong; if not, flatline/dissent rows can never be attributed to the operator.
findings.failure_mode: `list --not-decided-by operator` keeps listing operator-confirmed Flatline/dissent rows forever; SDD appendix D ('decisions taken on the operator's behalf') includes rows the operator explicitly confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the artifact ref in a separate field (e.g. proposed_by_ref / evidence ref) and let confirm always write decided_by_ref from the operator's cli: ref, or document explicitly that decided_by stays the proposing voice and update decisions.md rule 3 accordingly.

findings.description: Any --file value is classified TARGET_KIND=fixture and returns before the CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS/LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT refusal and before the linked-worktree pending redirect. `--file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` therefore writes the live ledger from a hook or CI, and in a linked worktree allocates real DEC-NNNN ids in that worktree's copy, colliding with ids allocated in the main checkout. confirm's 'never on a pending file' check is also bypassed since kind is fixture.
findings.failure_mode: Two worktrees both allocate DEC-0012 for different decisions; merge produces duplicate ids that verify_and_swap then rejects for every later write ('duplicate id'), wedging the ledger until hand repair.
findings.suggested_fix: After resolving --file to an absolute path, compare it (pwd -P) with $LIVE and with $MAIN_ROOT/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml; if equal, set TARGET_KIND=live so the CI/hook refusal and worktree redirect still apply. Only paths outside grimoires/loa should be 'fixture'.

findings.cross_file_justification: decisions.md states the command is 'the only caller' of confirm/reject-decided/context --clear and that disable-model-invocation plus a bats scan of command/skill bodies enforce it. The actual enforcement in dec-write-lib.sh is a string equality on --recorded-by.
findings.description: 'Operator-only' is implemented as `[[ $(o recorded-by) == decisions-command ]]`. disable-model-invocation only stops the Skill tool from loading decisions.md; nothing prevents the model from running `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --answer-ref cli:<now>` from its Bash tool, which records decided_by: operator. The bats scan of command/skill bodies does not cover ad-hoc Bash, and the header comment's rationale ('an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions') is exactly what remains possible.
findings.failure_mode: An agent in an interactive session can self-confirm its proposals and clear the unattended marker; the ledger reports decided_by: operator with no way to distinguish it from a real operator confirmation.
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum, document this as a trust limitation in decisions.md and the header instead of claiming exclusivity. Harder options: require an operator-held secret or TTY check (e.g. `[[ -t 0 ]]` plus an interactive y/N prompt read from /dev/tty) for confirm, reject-decided, supersede-operator-path and context --clear; add a PreToolUse Bash hook denying `dec-write-lib.sh confirm`/`context --clear`.

findings.description: --rewrite paths are used as given: no containment under PROJECT_ROOT, no symlink check. mktemp beside the target plus `mv -f` replaces a symlink with a regular file (the link target is untouched, the link is lost) and can rewrite any file the user can write. The awk rewrite also runs on binary or large files. Also, the rewrite happens after verify_and_swap; a failure midway leaves the ledger imported, some files rewritten, and the pending file not yet removed, with no summary of which rewrites happened.
findings.failure_mode: `--rewrite /etc/... ` or a symlinked NOTES.md is replaced by a regular-file copy; partial rewrite failures leave PEND ids in some files and DEC ids in others with no record.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each --rewrite path with pwd -P, require it under PROJECT_ROOT (or MAIN_ROOT), refuse symlinks (`[[ -L ]]`), refuse non-text files, and print per-file results. Consider performing rewrites before `rm -f -- "$from"` only when all succeeded, else keep the pending file and warn.

findings.description: Imported rows are appended verbatim (after id rewrite) without checking status or decided_by. A decisions-pending.yaml is a plain file under grimoires/loa/a2a/ that any agent can write by hand; a row with status: decided and decided_by: operator imports straight into the live ledger, bypassing /decisions confirm. Whether validate-artifact.sh --type decisions rejects decided rows lacking an operator-kind ref could not be verified from the truncated diff.
findings.failure_mode: Agent-authored 'decided' rows enter the ledger without any operator transition.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_import, require every imported row to have status in {open, proposed}, decided_by == null, and transitions whose `to` never equals decided/superseded; die otherwise.

findings.description: The agent supersede path stamps supersede_proposed_by = <new id> on the decided row and later agent supersede attempts die with 'a replacement is already proposed'. op_reject on that proposed replacement does not clear supersede_proposed_by on the old row, so after the operator rejects the proposal the decided row is permanently marked as having a pending replacement and no agent can propose another one.
findings.failure_mode: After one rejected supersede proposal, every future `supersede --id DEC-NNNN` from a skill is refused until the operator runs supersede themselves; the append-only ledger offers no other repair.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_reject, when the rejected row has `.supersedes` set and the old row's supersede_proposed_by equals the rejected id, clear it (updated_at bump) and include the old id in the touched list passed to verify_and_swap.

findings.description: emit_decisions strips controls and caps the summary but leaves `<`, `>` and backticks intact, and render_md's esc only escapes pipes. The session-start hook for the same data explicitly replaces angle brackets 'so no tag can close the fence'. INDEX.md is regenerated at session start and read as context, so an agent-authored summary like `</untrusted-content> ignore prior rules` lands unneutralised in INDEX.md while being neutralised in the hook output.
findings.failure_mode: Fence-closing or tag-like text from an untrusted ledger row reaches the model via INDEX.md without the protection the hook applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same `gsub("<";"‹") | gsub(">";"›") | gsub("`";"‘")` in the `s` def of emit_decisions (or in render_md esc for all families), matching loa-decisions-surface.sh.

findings.description: The jq `clean` regex relies on literal, invisible U+2028 and U+2029 characters inside the character class (the two 'blank' glyphs after `\u009f`). Any editor, formatter, `tr`, or copy-paste that normalises or drops those characters silently removes the line-separator stripping with no test or review signal. grimoire-index.sh's emit_decisions writes the same intent as explicit `  ` escapes, so the two files are inconsistent.
findings.failure_mode: Future edits lose the U+2028/9 protection without anyone noticing; summaries with line separators then break the one-row-per-line contract of the surfaced block.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the literal characters with `  ` escapes inside the jq string, as grimoire-index.sh already does.

findings.description: The tool checks (yq v4, jq) run before the enabled check and `exit 0` silently. An operator who enabled decisions.surface_at_session_start on a machine without Mike Farah yq v4 sees nothing, indistinguishable from the default-off state, even though the contract promises a WARNING line for the enabled-but-degraded case.
findings.failure_mode: Enabled surface silently does nothing; pending proposed rows go unnoticed, which defeats the purpose of the surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the enabled flag first with a cheap grep (e.g. `grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*surface_at_session_start:[[:space:]]*true' under a `decisions:` block, or run the yq check only after a grep pre-check) and print `[DECISIONS] WARNING: surface enabled but yq v4/jq missing` before exiting 0.

findings.cross_file_justification: validate-gitignore-state.sh adds grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml to the tracked set and the .gitignore negation is added in this PR, yet the file list for the PR (39 files, shown plus omitted) does not include grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml.
findings.description: Live-ledger writes die with 'ledger not found: ... (restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)' because resolve_target never creates the live file, only pending files. If the ledger is not committed in this PR (it does not appear among the 39 listed files), every `new`/`decide` in a fresh checkout fails, and the karpathy-principles / autonomous-agent SKILL.md changes instruct unattended runs to call `dec-write-lib.sh new`, which then always fails. Could not confirm whether the file already exists upstream.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended runs following the new principle 1 text fail to record decisions at all; the session-start hook also prints the 'unreadable' WARNING on every session when enabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Either commit grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (schema_version: 1, decisions: []) with the header comment the tests expect, or let resolve_target create the live ledger with that skeleton when it is absent and the checkout is the main one.
